editorial:
Imagine being a young artist who just wants to make music that actually means something to people. You get to follow Nie Er, a passionate musician who finds himself caught up in the middle of a huge political struggle. The movie feels like a journey through a very tense time in history, focusing on how one man's creativity can spark a whole movement. It is not just a dry history lesson; it feels more like a personal story about friendship and fighting for what you believe in while the world is falling apart around you.

What really works here is how the music is woven into the plot, making you feel the energy of the crowds. The acting is solid, though some of the slower parts might feel a bit long if you are not into dramas. If you love stories about underdogs and artistic passion, you will really enjoy this.
endingExplained: The story wraps up with the emotional completion of the song March of the Volunteers. You see how the music becomes a symbol of strength and unity for the people fighting for their country. While Nie Er does not get to see the full long-term impact of his work because he dies young, the movie shows that his voice lives on. It ends by connecting his hard work to the official national anthem used today.
targetAudience: Ideal for anyone who loves historical stories and music.
